# Caption Translator

- Route: `/tools/caption-translator`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `ai`
- Slug: `caption-translator`

## Summary

Translate SRT and VTT subtitle files while preserving cue timings, cue order, and structure — no third-party AI provider. (AI tools)

## Details

Translate existing subtitle files between languages without ever touching the cue timing. Media Manipulator parses the cues from your .srt or .vtt file, translates only the text using our locally-hosted caption translation model, and re-emits the original timestamps verbatim. No third-party translation API sees your captions — the model runs on our own GPU server.
### What it does
- Accepts .srt or .vtt caption files and produces a translated copy in the same format (or the opposite, if you choose).
- Preserves cue numbers, cue order, and timestamps exactly — only the cue text is translated.
- Runs translation on our local Ollama model server using a custom captions-tuned model — your captions never leave our infrastructure.
- Supports 30+ target languages including major European, Asian, and Middle-Eastern languages.
### How to use it
1. Upload .srt or .vtt: Drop your existing subtitle file into the uploader.
2. Pick languages: Auto-detect or pick a source language, then choose a target language.
3. We translate cue text: Our local AI translates only the caption text — timestamps and ordering stay frozen.
4. Download translated captions: Get back a clean .srt or .vtt with identical timing and a translated copy of every cue.
### Supported formats
- Input: srt, vtt
- Output: srt, vtt
- Translation runs on a locally-hosted Ollama model — no third-party translation API is contacted.
- NOTE and STYLE blocks in WebVTT files are preserved as-is.
### Technical details
- Translation runs on our own Ollama server using a captions-tuned derivative of Translate-Gemma (mm-captions-translategemma-12b).
- We send only the cue text + a strict JSON schema header to the model and pin the timing back from the original file when reading the response — so even a misbehaving model cannot corrupt your cue timing.
- NOTE and STYLE blocks in VTT files are preserved and never sent to the translator.
- For long subtitle tracks we batch cues so the model never approaches its context limit.
### Use cases
- Multilingual YouTube channels: Translate one master English SRT into 5+ languages for the same upload.
- Online courses: Reach international students with subtitles in their native language.
- Documentary / film festivals: Prepare translation tracks without touching cue timing.
- News and journalism: Translate breaking-news caption tracks while keeping precise sync.
### FAQ
Q: Can I translate an SRT file without breaking timestamps?
A: Yes — that is the whole point of this tool. We parse the cues, translate only the text, and then pin the original timestamps back exactly before writing the output.
Q: What subtitle formats are supported?
A: Both SubRip (.srt) and WebVTT (.vtt) are supported. You can keep the output format the same as the input or convert between them.
Q: Can I translate captions for YouTube videos?
A: Yes. Generate (or export) an SRT from your video, translate it here, and upload the new SRT as an additional language track on YouTube.
Q: Are captions translated with a third-party AI provider?
A: No. The translation runs on our own Ollama-hosted model — your captions never leave our infrastructure.
Q: What happens to cue timing?
A: Cue start and end times are preserved exactly — we pin them back from the original file after translation so even a misbehaving model cannot corrupt your timing.
